about.chapters.work.title: What I actually do
about.chapters.work.body: I started by taking things apart to see how they worked: HTML and CSS, then Python scripts that could recognize a face in a photo or cut up a video automatically. That habit never really left. Give me a repetitive process and I'd rather spend a week automating it than a year doing it by hand. These days that shows up as full-stack work: building the interface, the system behind it, and the automation that ties the two together.
about.chapters.method.title: How I get there
about.chapters.method.body: I don't start from the interface. I start from the process it's supposed to replace: what's manual, what's error-prone, what someone's doing by hand that a system could do better. Rendr came out of exactly that, watching a pipeline that needed a person babysitting it and building the thing that didn't. I'd rather ship a system that runs on its own than a demo that only works when I'm the one driving it.
about.chapters.learning.title: What I'm still learning
about.chapters.learning.body: Focus, mostly. I've gone from computer-vision experiments to e-commerce pages to automation to Rendr, and each one taught me something the last one didn't, but breadth has a cost. The skill I'm actively building now is choosing one hard problem and staying with it long enough to actually finish it.
about.pull: If a computer can do it, it shouldn't be my job to do it twice.
about.timeline.heading: The short chronology
about.timeline.1.title: First lines of code
about.timeline.1.body: Started with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, then picked up React the same year.
about.timeline.2.title: Python, and CS50
about.timeline.2.body: Taught myself Python and dabbled in C++, building small computer-vision projects (face and object recognition, video manipulation) and finishing Harvard's CS50.
about.timeline.3.title: Practice, then projects of my own
about.timeline.3.body: Kept coding through school, sharpening problem-solving on Codewars, then started building e-commerce landing pages and experimenting with video automation on the side.
about.timeline.4.title: Rendr, and a computer-science degree
about.timeline.4.body: Dropped the landing pages to build Rendr. Now in my third year of a computer-science degree (MIAGE) at Université Évry Paris-Saclay, Rendr still running alongside it, and a summer spent working as a cashier in Brittany: living on my own, on my own income, for the first time.
about.timeline.5.title: What's next
about.timeline.5.body: Looking for an internship required by my program, and aiming to finish my master's degree.
about.signoff: If any of that sounds like the kind of work you need doing, I'd like to hear about it.

home.hero.lede: Building since 2020: interfaces, the systems behind them, and the automation that connects the two.
home.hero.bio: I build full-stack apps, and specialize in solid systems that apps can grow and scale on. I also love building automations for any repetitive task, app, or system I run into.
home.hero.tagline: I'd rather automate it than do it twice.
home.hero.blurb: Started with Python scripts that could recognize a face in a photo, ended up building systems other software depends on. I like taking a process someone's doing by hand and turning it into something nobody has to think about again.

home.terminal.prompts.build.label: What do you build?
home.terminal.prompts.build.answers.1: Full-stack systems: the backend, the interface on top, and the automation connecting them.
home.terminal.prompts.build.answers.2: Mostly things that replace a repetitive process. If a human's doing it by hand, I'd rather write the script.
home.terminal.prompts.build.answers.3: Web apps and the automation behind them. A video-automation project is the biggest one right now.
home.terminal.prompts.build.answers.4: Systems that don't need me standing next to them once they're running.
home.terminal.prompts.build.answers.5: Interfaces, APIs, and the automation nobody asked for but everybody ends up needing.
home.terminal.prompts.stack.label: Tech stack?
home.terminal.prompts.stack.answers.1: JavaScript, Node, React, and React Native for mobile. HTML, CSS and Sass underneath it all, Python when it's about automation or data.
home.terminal.prompts.stack.answers.2: Mostly JavaScript end to end: React and React Native up front, Node on the back, Sass for styling.
home.terminal.prompts.stack.answers.3: Whatever the project needs, really. I pick up a new language fast when a task calls for it.
home.terminal.prompts.stack.answers.4: HTML, CSS and Sass for the layer people see, JavaScript and Node underneath, Python for scripts and automation.
home.terminal.prompts.stack.answers.5: A mix: JS and Python most days, but I'll learn and ship in whatever a task actually requires.
